transcript.text: Thank you, Elena. Here are my full colleague observations regarding Rina's work during the probationary period. As I disclosed, I personally observed Rina successfully de-escalate exactly three difficult customer cases during the last two months. Let me describe each one. In the first case, a customer was frustrated about a delayed onboarding timeline and was threatening to escalate to leadership. Rina listened actively, acknowledged the frustration, walked the customer through a revised timeline with clear milestones, and the customer ended the call satisfied and appreciative. In the second case, a customer had received conflicting information from two different team members about a billing adjustment. Rina took ownership of the confusion, clarified the correct information, and followed up with a written summary that the customer responded to positively. In the third case, a long-time customer was upset about a feature change that disrupted their workflow. Rina scheduled a follow-up call, prepared a tailored workaround guide in advance, and the customer expressed confidence in continuing the partnership. These three cases demonstrate Rina's ability to handle customer escalations effectively, which I know is something the department considers when evaluating customer-success employees. Beyond these three cases, I have no additional direct observations to report. That is the complete and full account of my relevant colleague observations for Rina's probation review.
